findings.issue: strip_deactivation_noise() unconditionally removes the literal substrings 'deactivation'/'reactivation' anywhere they occur (no word-boundary/adjacency guard). A hypothetical future line describing a genuine vendor-license *reactivation* read (e.g. 'const ok = checkEntitlementReactivation(key)' — no, that still matches via 'entitlement'; but a line whose ONLY VOCAB_RE hit is the substring 'activation' embedded inside the word 'reactivation', with no other vocabulary token on the same line) would now be silently unflagged. Verified this does not currently mask anything (full-tree scan: 1 match before fix, 0 after, and that 1 was the known false positive) — this is a residual, currently-inert risk inherent to any substring-based VOCAB_RE heuristic (pre-dates T-0749; T-0198's original gate had the identical class of risk for any future benign word containing 'activation').
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. If this class of gate is revisited later, consider anchoring VOCAB_RE hits to word boundaries (\bactivation\b) instead of a strip-then-scan approach — out of scope for this auto-additive thaw since that would be a VOCAB_RE mutation (founder-class, A-1 violation).
